---
title: Waiting for email
description: Polling, timeouts, and matchers for reliably receiving a message in a test.
---

Email delivery takes a few hundred milliseconds in the sandbox and a few seconds through real providers. Tests should **wait**, not sleep.

## Use the wait endpoint

[Wait for message](/api/inboxes/wait-for-message) holds the request open until a matching message arrives or the timeout passes, then returns the message.

<Tabs>
<Tab label="TypeScript">
```typescript
const message = await inbox.messages.wait({
  subject: /verify your account/i,
  timeout: 30_000,
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab label="Python">
```python
message = inbox.messages.wait(subject=r"verify your account", timeout=30)
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Matchers

| Matcher           | Matches                                   |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `subjectContains` | Case-insensitive substring of the subject |
| `from`            | Exact sender address                      |
| `bodyMatches`     | Regular expression over the text body     |
| `hasAttachment`   | At least one attachment                   |

All present matchers must match; see the [MessageMatcher](/api/inboxes/wait-for-message#request-body) schema.

## Timeouts

<Callout type="tip">
Start with 30 seconds in CI and 10 seconds locally. A timeout returns `408`, which most test runners surface with the request details.
</Callout>

## Avoid

- Sleeping a fixed number of seconds before reading the inbox.
- Reusing one inbox across tests that run in parallel.
- Matching on the whole HTML body; match on the text body or a link instead.
